title: Marketing Fundamentals - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Analyze Buying Behavior
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Business-to-Business (B2B) marketing differs from Business-to-Consumer (B2C) marketing primarily because:
options: B2B purchases are typically smaller in financial volume and less complex.
B2B involves purchasing goods for use in operations or resale, whereas B2C purchases are for personal use.
B2C buyers typically use more rational and profit-driven motives than B2B buyers.
B2B marketing strictly relies on television advertising.
questions.explain: B2B markets involve organizations purchasing goods to produce other goods, support daily operations, or for resale. B2C involves individuals purchasing items for personal consumption.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A consumer buying a cup of coffee every morning on the way to work is an example of which type of decision-making process?
questions.explain: Routine decision making is used when buying frequently purchased, low-cost items that require little search or decision effort.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Purchasing a home or a new automobile typically requires a high degree of research and consumer involvement. This is known as:
questions.explain: Extensive decision making occurs when a consumer is buying an unfamiliar, expensive, or infrequently bought item and requires significant information searching.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Emotional buying motives are primarily based on:
options: Feelings, social approval, fear, or prestige.
Cost savings and return on investment.
questions.explain: Emotional motives depend on feelings or attitudes toward a product rather than logical reasons.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Rational buying motives are driven by:
options: Logic, saving money, or product dependability.
questions.explain: Rational motives involve logical considerations such as price, efficiency, safety, and dependability.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a psychological factor that heavily influences consumer buying behavior?
questions.explain: Consumer behavior is driven by psychological factors like motivation, perception, learning, and beliefs/attitudes. Culture and family fall under social and cultural factors.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: In buyer behavior, cognitive dissonance refers to:
options: The confusion a customer feels when faced with too many similar product choices.
Post-purchase doubt or anxiety about whether the right buying decision was made.
The difference between a product's manufacturing cost and its final retail price.
A competitor's negative advertising campaign causing market disruption.
questions.explain: Cognitive dissonance is the inner tension a consumer experiences after recognizing an inconsistency between behavior and values or opinions, commonly felt as 'buyer's remorse'.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: How do reference groups influence individual buying behavior?
options: They control the product supply chain and limit availability.
They serve as a point of comparison or role models, shaping an individual's attitudes and choices.
They strictly establish retail product pricing for a demographic.
They distribute the product directly to niche consumer groups.
questions.explain: A reference group is any group that individuals use as a standard for evaluating themselves and their own behavior, which highly influences what they buy.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: According to Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, which type of needs must be satisfied first before a consumer begins to focus on prestige or self-actualization?
questions.explain: Maslow theorized that basic physiological needs must be met before an individual seeks higher-level emotional and psychological needs.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which statement best describes an impulse purchase?
options: A planned purchase made after extensive research and budgeting.
Buying a product in large, wholesale bulk quantities.
An unplanned decision to buy a product or service made just before the moment of purchase.
A long-term B2B procurement contract between two corporations.
questions.explain: An impulse purchase is a sudden, spontaneous, and unplanned buying decision, often triggered by emotions or store displays.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA
